boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named downtown and near-campus destinations, each tied to its surrounding corridor.

cards.title: Cortland Free Library
cards.subtitle: Church Street corridor, one block west of Main Street
cards.notes: Enter from the Court Street side for elevator access, then use the public reading areas or borrow materials during posted library hours.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop on the Church and Court streets block.
cards.evidence_claim: The library is located at 32 Church Street; its site lists public hours and identifies the Court Street entrance for elevator accessibility.
cards.source_title: Location, Hours & Contact – Cortland Free Library
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before going; the site notes that weather closings can affect service.

cards.title: Cortland City Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor, in front of City Hall
cards.notes: Plan this stop for a listed Tuesday or Saturday market day and browse the vendors in front of City Hall at Court and Church streets.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled downtown market on the Court Street civic block.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Cortland places the market at 25 Court Street, in front of City Hall at the corner of Court and Church, and lists Tuesday and Saturday market times.
cards.access_notes: The listing gives Tuesdays and Saturdays, 8 a.m.–2 p.m.; confirm that the market is operating before making the trip.

cards.title: City of Cortland City Hall
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor, beside Fire Headquarters
cards.notes: Use this civic-block landmark as an orientation point, and check the city calendar or department pages before visiting for a specific public-service need.
cards.short_summary: The city-government anchor at 25 Court Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Cortland lists its contact address as 25 Court Street, Cortland, NY 13045.
cards.access_notes: This is an active government building; consult the relevant city department for visitor procedures or meeting details.

cards.title: Cortland Fire Headquarters
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor, next to City Hall
cards.notes: View the historic exterior from the public street and keep driveways and apparatus access clear; use the department site for public programs or contact details.
cards.short_summary: A 1914 firehouse on the Court Street civic block.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland Fire Department identifies its headquarters at 21 Court Street as a historic building constructed in 1914.
cards.access_notes: This is an operating emergency-services facility; observe from public areas and do not obstruct vehicles or entrances.

cards.title: Cortland County Courthouse
cards.subtitle: Greenbush Street corridor, off West Court Street
cards.notes: Use the public frontage as a Greenbush Street landmark; if entering for court business, review the court’s accessibility and building information first.
cards.short_summary: A county-court destination on the Greenbush Street block.
cards.evidence_claim: New York Courts lists the Cortland County Courthouse at 46 Greenbush Street and describes elevators, public parking, restrooms, and an ADA-accessible entrance.
cards.source_title: CORTLAND COUNTY - Courthouse | New York Courts
cards.access_notes: Court access and security procedures can vary; confirm the relevant court office’s requirements before entering.

cards.title: Suggett House Museum
cards.subtitle: Homer Avenue corridor, near the downtown civic blocks
cards.notes: Check the museum’s exhibit schedule, then join a guided tour to see county-history artifacts in the former Suggett family home.
cards.short_summary: A local-history museum housed in the Suggett family home.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland County Historical Society states that the Suggett House Museum holds its artifacts and tells Cortland County history through exhibits; it lists guided tours Wednesday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Suggett House | Cortland County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: The Historical Society lists guided tours Wednesday–Saturday, 12–5 p.m.; verify exhibit and tour availability before going.

cards.title: All My Friends Books
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, downtown Cortland
cards.notes: Browse new and used books, stationery, and bookish gifts, or check the shop calendar for an in-store event before heading to 51 Main Street.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages independent bookstore on Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: All My Friends Books identifies its Cortland shop at 51 Main Street and describes it as a general-interest, all-ages independent bookstore with new and used books.
cards.source_title: All My Friends Books | Indie Bookstores in Cortland & Skaneateles, NY
cards.access_notes: The shop lists daily hours on its website; check for updates and event-specific timing before visiting.

cards.title: The Local Food Market & Cafe
cards.subtitle: North Main Street corridor, downtown Cortland
cards.notes: Use this Main Street stop for a market-and-cafe visit, and check the business directly for its current menu, service details, and availability.
cards.short_summary: A named food-market and cafe destination on North Main.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland County Convention & Visitors Bureau lists The Local Food Market at 37 Main Street in Cortland.
cards.source_title: The Port Watson Mini-Conference Center | Experience Cortland
cards.access_notes: Confirm current hours and offerings with the business before visiting.

cards.title: Lot 1 Vintage
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, downtown Cortland
cards.notes: Add this storefront to a Main Street walk if you want to browse vintage goods; verify current opening information with the shop before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A named vintage storefront on the Main Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025 Cortland Travel Guide lists Lot 1 Vintage at 79 Main Street, Cortland, with its website.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the shop’s current hours and access arrangements directly before visiting.

cards.title: Squires Block Clock Tower
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor at Port Watson Street
cards.notes: Pause at the Main and Port Watson streets corner to photograph the clock-tower building, then use the historical society account to trace the site’s earlier uses.
cards.short_summary: A documented clock-tower landmark at a downtown Main Street corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland County Historical Society states that the Squires Block, with its iconic clock tower, replaced the Eagle Store at the Main and Port Watson streets corner in 1883.
cards.source_title: Main Street – City of Cortland | Cortland County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: View and photograph the exterior from public sidewalks while observing traffic conditions at the Main and Port Watson streets corner.
